nodeData.note: How individuals in Kenya get a KRA PIN, file the yearly return on iTax, pay any tax due and avoid penalties. Simple steps for employees, bookkeepers and small business owners.

children.topic: What iTax is and why it matters
children.note: iTax is KRA's online system for registering, filing returns and paying tax. Almost every working adult in Kenya with a KRA PIN uses it at least once a year.
A KRA PIN is your personal tax number from the Kenya Revenue Authority. You need it for a job, a bank account, a business licence and to file returns.

manas.q: What is a KRA PIN?

children.note: You apply for a PIN online on iTax using your ID details. Once you have it, you keep the same PIN for life.
iTax is KRA's website for tax work: you log in with your PIN and password, file returns, generate payment slips and download certificates.

manas.q: What is iTax?

children.note: Filing on time keeps you free of penalties. A compliant tax record also helps when you need a tender, a loan or a Tax Compliance Certificate.
Filing a return means telling KRA your income and tax. Paying is a separate step. You can file on time and still owe a late payment penalty if you do not pay.

manas.q: Is filing a return the same as paying tax?

children.note: The basic rule is simple: if you have a KRA PIN, you file every year, even when you earned nothing.
Every individual with a KRA PIN must file an individual income tax return every year, even with no income (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Who must file an individual income tax return in Kenya?

children.note: Returns for a year of income can be filed from 1 January to 30 June of the next year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When can you file your individual return for a year of income?

children.note: The deadline for the individual return is 30 June of the year after the year of income (check the current KRA rate). For 2025 income, that is 30 June 2026.

manas.q: What is the deadline for individual income tax returns?

children.note: The year of income for individuals is the calendar year, January to December. You file for last year's income in the first half of this year.
People who are exempt from tax must still file a return and enter their Exemption Certificate Number (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Do exempt persons need to file a return?

children.note: For persons with disability, the first KES 150,000 of monthly income is exempt (check the current KRA rate). They file using their Exemption Certificate Number.
Non-residents do not get personal relief (check the current KRA rate). Their tax works differently, so check with KRA or a tax adviser.
There are three common cases: employment income only, employment plus other income, and no income at all (NIL).
Most employees have only a salary. Your employer has already deducted PAYE every month, so the return mostly confirms those figures.
The P9 is your employer's tax deduction card for the year. It shows your pay and the tax deducted. Ask HR or payroll for it early.

manas.q: What is a P9 form?

children.note: Log in to iTax, choose the income tax return for residents, and enter or confirm your pay and tax from the P9. Then submit and save the receipt.
iTax may show your employer's figures already filled in. Check them against your P9 and payslips before you submit.
If you changed jobs, you need a P9 from each employer. Personal relief is claimed once, so you may end up owing a little tax.
If you also earn rent, business profit or side-hustle income, you must add it to the return and work out any extra tax.
Examples: profit from a duka, a matatu, consulting fees, or farm income. Each source is declared on the return.
Work out profit from your sales and expenses records. Guessing leads to errors that KRA can query later.
When other income is added, the total tax is often more than PAYE already paid. The difference is tax due, paid by the deadline.
A NIL return says you had no taxable income for the year. It is the quickest return to file.
File a NIL return if you have a PIN but earned no income in the year (check the current KRA rate). Students and the unemployed often need this.

manas.q: When do you file a NIL return?

children.note: NIL returns can be filed on iTax or on the KRA M-Service App (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Where can you file a NIL return?

children.note: If you had a salary, even for part of the year, a NIL return is wrong. File an employment return with your P9 instead.
An exempt person files the normal return and enters the Exemption Certificate Number given by KRA.
iTax gives an acknowledgement receipt. Save it as proof of filing. If tax is due, the next step is generating a payment slip.

children.topic: Reliefs and how tax is worked out
children.note: Your tax is worked out using tax bands, then reliefs are taken off. Knowing this helps you check your P9.
Annual bands: first 288,000 at 10%; next 100,000 at 25%; next 5,612,000 at 30%; next 3,600,000 at 32.5%; above 9,600,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the annual individual tax bands?

children.note: Monthly bands: first 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly individual tax bands?

children.note: Personal relief is KES 28,800 a year, or 2,400 a month (check the current KRA rate). It is taken off the tax for resident individuals.

manas.q: How much is personal relief?

children.note: Insurance relief is 15% of premiums on life, education (10+ years) or health policies, up to KES 60,000 a year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How is insurance relief worked out?

children.note: Tax payable = tax from the bands minus reliefs. Then subtract PAYE already deducted to see if you owe more or nothing.

manas.q: How do you get tax payable from tax on bands?

children.note: After filing, any tax due is paid using a payment slip from iTax.
On iTax, choose to make a payment, pick the tax and period, and generate the slip (check the current KRA rate). The slip shows the amount and a Payment Registration Number.

manas.q: What do you need from iTax before paying tax?

children.note: The PRN is the reference number on your payment slip. It links your money to your tax so KRA can credit your account.

manas.q: What is a PRN?

children.note: Use M-Pesa Paybill 222222 (the unified Government paybill). The account number is the PRN on the slip (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How do you pay KRA tax by M-Pesa?

children.note: Take the slip to an appointed KRA bank and pay over the counter (check the current KRA rate). Keep the bank receipt.
Save the M-Pesa message or bank receipt with the slip. They are your proof if iTax does not show the payment.
Late filing and late payment are charged separately. You can be charged both.
For individuals: the higher of 5% of the tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate). Even a NIL filer can be charged the KES 2,000.

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for individuals?

children.note: If tax is paid after the due date: a penalty of 5% of the tax due (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the late payment penalty?

children.note: Interest of 1% per month is charged on unpaid tax until it is paid (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What interest does KRA charge on unpaid tax?

children.note: File by 30 June and pay by the same date. If you cannot pay in full, file anyway, so you avoid the late filing penalty.
Real numbers, step by step. Rates as confirmed on kra.go.ke today; always check the current KRA rate.
Mary earns KES 600,000 a year in salary. Let us work out her tax for the year.
117,400 − personal relief 28,800 = KES 88,600 tax for the year (check the current KRA rate).
If her P9 shows PAYE of 88,600, she owes nothing more. This is a simplified example that ignores other deductions.
Late filing penalty is the higher of 5% of tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 30,000 = 1,500. KES 2,000 is higher, so the penalty is KES 2,000.
5% × 100,000 = 5,000. That is higher than 2,000, so the penalty is KES 5,000.
Tax due is zero, so 5% is zero. The penalty is the minimum KES 2,000.
Otieno owes KES 60,000 on his duka profit. He files and pays 3 months after the deadline.
Higher of 5% × 60,000 = 3,000 or 2,000. Penalty = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 60,000 = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
1% × 60,000 × 3 months = KES 1,800 (check the current KRA rate).
60,000 + 3,000 + 3,000 + 1,800 = KES 67,800. Filing and paying on time would have saved KES 7,800.
Jane pays health and life premiums. See how the KES 60,000 cap works (check the current KRA rate).
15% × 48,000 = 7,200. Below 60,000, so her relief is KES 7,200 for the year.
15% × 500,000 = 75,000. That is above the cap, so relief is limited to KES 60,000.
Good records make filing quick and protect you if KRA asks questions.
P9 forms, payslips, filing receipts, payment slips, M-Pesa or bank receipts, insurance premium certificates and business sales and expense records.
For a duka or matatu, keep daily sales, receipts for expenses and bank or M-Pesa statements. These support the profit you declare.
Make one folder, paper or on your phone, for each year of income. File everything as it comes in.
Keep your PIN and password safe and private. Never share your password, even with a cyber café attendant.
These errors cause most penalties and KRA queries for ordinary filers.
People with no income think they need not file. They do, and a late NIL return can still cost KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Can you be penalised for a late NIL return?

children.note: Forgetting insurance relief on a qualifying policy means paying more tax than you should. Keep the premium certificate.
Typing pay or PAYE that differs from the P9 can show tax due that is not real, or trigger a query. Copy figures carefully.
If you were employed, a NIL return is wrong. You must declare your employment income.
iTax gets busy near the deadline. File early in the window so problems can be fixed in time.
Submitting the return does not pay the tax. Generate the slip and pay, or penalty and interest will build up.
Businesses have more filings. This map covers the individual return; others have their own maps.
A sole trader declares business profit on their own individual return, together with any salary.
A company has its own KRA PIN and files a separate corporate return. See the corporate tax map.
A business registered for VAT files VAT returns separately. See the VAT map.
An employer files PAYE returns for staff. This is the employer's job, not the employee's. See the PAYE map.
Try each one, then open the bubble for the answer steps.
Wanjiku got a PIN for a job application but earned nothing last year. What should she file?
A NIL return, on iTax or the KRA M-Service App, by 30 June (check the current KRA rate).
Compute the late filing penalty when the tax due is KES 50,000.
Compare with KES 2,000. The higher is 2,500, so the penalty is KES 2,500 (check the current KRA rate).
What paybill and account number do you use to pay KRA by M-Pesa?
Paybill 222222; the account number is the PRN on your iTax payment slip (check the current KRA rate).
Short videos from KRA's own channels. Screens may change, so follow what you see on iTax today.

nodeData.note: eTIMS is KRA's free system for issuing electronic tax invoices. Almost every business in Kenya must use it, and since 2024 your business expenses only count for tax if backed by an eTIMS invoice (check the current KRA rule).

children.topic: What eTIMS is and why it matters
children.note: Start here: what the system is, who must use it and why your expenses depend on it.
eTIMS stands for electronic Tax Invoice Management System. It is free KRA software that sends each invoice you make to KRA as you issue it.

manas.q: What does eTIMS stand for?

children.note: You can use eTIMS on a computer, a phone or a tablet, so even a small duka owner can invoice from a phone.

manas.q: On which devices can eTIMS be used?

children.note: All persons in business must onboard and issue electronic tax invoices, whether or not they are VAT-registered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a business that is not VAT-registered use eTIMS?

children.note: Companies, partnerships, sole proprietors, associations and trusts are all covered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Which types of business must onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: People paying Monthly Rental Income tax, Turnover Tax or annual income tax on business income must onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Small informal traders, like a mama mboga or a boda boda business, are also expected to onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Suppliers whose services are exempt from VAT, like a hospital giving medical care or a school, must still onboard (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a VAT-exempt hospital or school onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: Since 1 January 2024 a business expense must be backed by an electronic tax invoice to be claimed for tax (check the current KRA rule). No eTIMS invoice usually means no deduction.

manas.q: From what date must a business expense be backed by an eTIMS invoice to be claimed?

children.note: KRA says eTIMS is free, runs on many devices, has a stock (inventory) module, keeps a record of all your invoices and makes filing returns simpler.

manas.q: Name four benefits of eTIMS that KRA lists.

children.note: KRA offers several ways (solutions) to use eTIMS. Pick the one that fits the size and setup of your business.
A web portal at etims.kra.go.ke where you log in and make invoices in the browser. Good for service businesses with few invoices.
Software you download for Windows or Android. It can handle several branches and tills, so it suits shops and pharmacies with many sales.
A simple web version reached through eCitizen. Handy for small traders who already use eCitizen.
Dial *222# on any phone to invoice. It is meant for individuals and sole proprietors, no smartphone or data needed.

manas.q: What is the eTIMS Lite USSD code, and who is it for?

children.note: An app from the Play Store or App Store for invoicing on a smartphone.
For businesses with their own invoicing or ERP system. The system is linked to KRA so invoices go to eTIMS automatically. VSCU and OSCU are the two integration types.

manas.q: Which eTIMS solution suits a business with its own invoicing system?

children.note: A special solution where the buyer, not the seller, makes the invoice. Covered in its own branch below.
You may register on more than one solution. Each has its own invoice number series, and all invoices show on your taxpayer portal (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: If you use two eTIMS solutions, do they share one invoice number series?

children.note: Onboarding means signing up your business on eTIMS. Steps differ a bit per solution; this is the general shape.
You need an active KRA PIN and your iTax login details before you start.
Decide which solution fits you: portal, Client, Lite (web, USSD or app) or system integration.
Register using your PIN on the chosen solution, e.g. on etims.kra.go.ke or eCitizen. Follow the on-screen steps.
KRA reviews the request; once approved you activate the solution and set up your device or till.
Load your products or services and regular customers so invoicing later is quick. The stock module can track goods.
Make your first real invoice and check that it appears on your taxpayer portal.
The daily work: making a sale invoice and correcting it with a credit note.
Your details, the buyer's PIN where they have one, the items, quantity, price and any VAT. eTIMS adds its own invoice number and sends it to KRA.
Business buyers need their PIN on your invoice so the expense counts for them. Always ask for it before you issue.
Log in, pick the customer, add items and quantities, check the VAT and total, then confirm. Print, share or send the invoice.
A credit note reduces or cancels an invoice already issued, for example when goods come back or a price was wrong.

manas.q: What is a credit note used for?

children.note: A credit note can only be raised from the same solution where the original invoice was made (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: From which eTIMS solution can a credit note be raised?

children.note: You cannot just erase a wrong invoice. You raise a credit note against it, then issue a correct new invoice.
Sometimes the seller is too small to invoice, so the buyer makes the invoice instead.
Where the seller is a small business or small-scale farmer with annual turnover not above KES 5 million, the buyer issues the invoice for them (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: When does the buyer issue the eTIMS invoice on the seller's behalf?

children.note: Buyer Initiated Invoicing is done through eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).
A Nakuru hotel buys KES 30,000 of sukuma from a small farmer. The hotel raises the invoice on eCitizen for the farmer, so the hotel's expense is backed.
Another option where the buyer generates the invoice instead of the seller. KRA offers it alongside BII in the same solution.

manas.q: What is reverse invoicing?

children.note: If you buy from small suppliers and nobody invoices, you lose the deduction. BII protects your own expense claim.

children.topic: Expenses that need no eTIMS invoice
children.note: Some costs are excluded from the eTIMS invoice rule (check the current KRA rule).
Staff pay is backed by payroll records, not an eTIMS invoice.
Imported goods have customs documents instead.
Airline tickets are excluded.
Capital allowances (investment deductions) are excluded.
Interest, and fees charged by financial institutions, are excluded.
Expenses already subject to final withholding tax are excluded.
Services from a non-resident with no permanent establishment in Kenya are excluded.
Remember: pay, imports, flights, investment allowances, interest and bank fees, final WHT, non-resident services.

manas.q: List the expenses excluded from needing an eTIMS invoice.

children.topic: Links to VAT and income tax
children.note: eTIMS invoices feed both your VAT return and your income tax computation.
The general VAT rate is 16% (check the current KRA rate). The old 8% rate on petroleum was deleted by the Finance Act 2023.

manas.q: What is Kenya's general VAT rate?

children.note: VAT charged on your sales invoices is output VAT, owed to KRA. eTIMS records it as you invoice.
VAT on your purchases is input VAT. Keep the supplier's eTIMS invoice as proof for any claim (check the current KRA rule).
Your eTIMS invoices are visible on the taxpayer portal, which makes filling the VAT return easier and helps match sales and purchases.
When working out taxable profit, an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice (and not excluded) is added back, so you pay more tax (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: What happens in the tax computation to an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice?

children.note: Before paying a supplier, check the invoice is a real eTIMS invoice with your PIN on it.
Wanjiku Supplies Ltd is VAT-registered. VAT is 16% (check the current KRA rate). Follow one sale, one credit note and one purchase.
Wanjiku sells goods for KES 50,000 plus VAT 8,000 (16%), total 58,000, and issues an eTIMS invoice.
Dr Receivables 58,000 / Cr Sales 50,000 / Cr VAT output 8,000. Debits 58,000 = credits 58,000.
The customer returns goods worth KES 10,000 before VAT. Wanjiku raises a credit note on the same eTIMS solution for 10,000 + VAT 1,600 = 11,600.
Dr Sales returns 10,000 / Dr VAT output 1,600 / Cr Receivables 11,600. Debits 11,600 = credits 11,600.
Wanjiku buys stationery for KES 20,000 + VAT 3,200 = 23,200. The supplier issues a valid eTIMS invoice with Wanjiku's PIN.
Dr Stationery expense 20,000 / Dr VAT input 3,200 / Cr Payables 23,200. Debits 23,200 = credits 23,200.
Output VAT 6,400 − input VAT 3,200 = KES 3,200 VAT payable to KRA.
If the stationery had no valid eTIMS invoice, the 20,000 is added back in the tax computation. Profit per books 40,000 − 20,000 = 20,000; taxable profit 40,000.
Errors that cost businesses money or cause trouble with KRA.

children.topic: Thinking only VAT payers need it
children.note: Wrong: all businesses must onboard, VAT-registered or not.
Paying a supplier on a handwritten receipt means the expense may not be deductible.
An invoice without the buyer's PIN does not help the buyer claim the cost.

children.topic: Credit note on the wrong solution
children.note: Trying to credit an invoice from a different solution fails. Use the solution where it was made.
Buying from small farmers without raising a buyer-initiated invoice loses the deduction.
Using an old rate or adding VAT to an exempt supply. Check the rate and item's VAT status.
Chasing an eTIMS invoice for salaries, bank charges or flights wastes time; these are excluded.
Try these, then open the steps.
Record a credit sale of KES 120,000 before VAT at 16%.
Dr Receivables 139,200 / Cr Sales 120,000 / Cr VAT output 19,200. Balances at 139,200.
A pharmacy pays KES 15,000 bank charges and KES 40,000 for cleaning with only a cash receipt. Which is deductible?
Fees of financial institutions are excluded from the rule, so the 15,000 can be claimed.
Cleaning needs an eTIMS invoice. With only a cash receipt, the 40,000 is added back.
A school buys maize from a farmer with turnover of KES 2 million. Who issues the invoice?
Turnover is not above KES 5 million, so the school (buyer) issues it through Buyer Initiated Invoicing on eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).

nodeData.note: How to run a monthly payroll in Kenya: gross pay, NSSF, SHIF, housing levy and PAYE, the payslip, the journal, and paying and filing on time.

children.topic: What payroll is and why it matters
children.note: Payroll is the monthly job of working out what each worker earns, taking off the legal deductions, paying them and sending the deductions to the government bodies.
Pay staff the right net amount, and pass the deductions to KRA, NSSF and SHA on time.

manas.q: What is payroll, in one sentence?

children.note: The law makes the employer the tax collector for its staff. Money deducted belongs to KRA, NSSF or SHA, not to the business.
Any business with staff: a duka with two shop attendants, a matatu owner paying a driver, or a hospital with 200 nurses.
Topic 1 showed how to log in and file on KRA iTax. Payroll uses the same iTax account to file the monthly PAYE return.
Late or wrong deductions bring penalties and interest from KRA and the other bodies, and unhappy staff. Being on time is cheaper.
The same six steps happen every month. Follow them in order and payroll becomes routine.
Gather basic salaries, overtime, allowances, new joiners, leavers and advances before the cut-off date.
Add basic pay, allowances, overtime and taxable benefits to get gross pay for each worker.
Work out NSSF, SHIF, housing levy, then PAYE, then any other deductions like loans or SACCO savings.
A manager checks the payroll report, then net pay goes out by bank transfer or M-Pesa bulk payment.
Send PAYE and the other deductions to the right bodies and file the P10 PAYE return on iTax.
Post the payroll journal in the books, give payslips, and keep the records safe.
PAYE must be deducted, paid and the return filed by the 9th of the following month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: By when must PAYE be paid and the P10 return filed?

children.note: Gross pay is everything the worker earns before any deduction. It is the starting point for every calculation.
Basic salary plus allowances, overtime, commission, bonus and taxable benefits for the month.

manas.q: What is gross pay?

children.note: House, transport and lunch allowances paid in cash are part of gross pay and are taxed like salary.
Things given instead of cash, such as a company car, free housing or school fees paid for the worker.
Non-cash benefits become taxable when their total value is above KES 5,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When do non-cash benefits become taxable?

children.note: What the worker actually receives: gross pay minus all deductions.

manas.q: What is net pay?

children.note: Four deductions are set by law. Three come off before PAYE is worked out; PAYE is calculated last.
The National Social Security Fund saves for retirement. Worker and employer each pay 6% of pay (check the current KRA rate).
6% on pay up to the Lower Earnings Limit of KES 9,000, so at most KES 540 each side (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier I (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: 6% on pay from KES 9,001 up to the Upper Earnings Limit of KES 108,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier II (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: Tier I and Tier II together cap at KES 6,480 for the worker and the same for the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the maximum NSSF per side each month?

children.note: The employer pays the same amount as the worker on top of salary. It is a business cost, not a deduction.
The Social Health Insurance Fund, run by the Social Health Authority (SHA), funds health care.
2.75% of gross salary, with a minimum of KES 300 and no upper cap (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the SHIF rate?

children.note: SHIF is a contribution from the employee. The employer deducts it and sends it to SHA.
A levy that funds affordable housing. Both the worker and the employer pay.
1.5% of gross pay from the worker, plus a matching 1.5% from the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the Affordable Housing Levy rate?

children.note: Remit within 9 working days after the end of the month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When must the housing levy be remitted?

children.note: Pay As You Earn is income tax taken from salary each month and paid to KRA.
First 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly PAYE bands?

children.note: Every resident worker gets KES 2,400 a month taken off the tax (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How much is monthly personal relief?

children.note: 15% of qualifying insurance premiums, up to KES 60,000 a year, also reduces tax (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is insurance relief?

children.note: Housing levy, SHIF, registered pension/NSSF up to KES 30,000 a month and post-retirement medical fund up to KES 15,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Which items are deducted before PAYE is calculated?

children.note: Always calculate in the same order. Doing PAYE first is the most common beginner mistake.
Start with total gross pay for the month.
Work out the employee NSSF, SHIF and housing levy from gross pay.
Gross pay minus the allowed items (NSSF, SHIF, AHL) gives taxable pay.

manas.q: How do you get taxable pay?

children.note: Apply the PAYE bands to taxable pay, slice by slice, and add the slices.
Take off personal relief (and any insurance relief). The answer is PAYE, never below zero.
Gross pay minus NSSF, SHIF, AHL, PAYE and other deductions gives net pay.

manas.q: What is the net pay formula?

children.note: Two full payrolls in KES using today's rates (check the current KRA rate). Every figure is checked and the journals balance.
A hospital pharmacist earns KES 100,000 a month with no benefits.

nodeData.note: Practical Excel for people working in accounts: a clean sheet, the formulas you need daily, pivot tables, reconciliations, ageing debtors, a loan schedule and how to check your work.

children.note: Most accounting jobs in Kenya use Excel every day, even where there is an accounting system. It is where you clean, check and explain the numbers.
A grid of cells where you type data and formulas, so the sheet does the sums for you and redoes them when the data changes.

manas.q: What is Excel, in one sentence?

children.note: Bank and M-Pesa reconciliations, debtor lists, sales summaries, budgets, loan schedules and reports for the boss.
iTax, eTIMS and payroll all give you downloads (CSV or Excel). This topic shows how to tidy and check those files.
Six March 2026 sales: Nairobi M-Pesa 12,500; Mombasa cash 8,200; Nairobi cash 4,300; Nairobi M-Pesa 7,750; Mombasa M-Pesa 15,000; Kisumu cash 6,250. Total KES 54,000.
A tidy layout makes every formula, filter and pivot table work first time. Messy sheets cause most errors.
Each row is one sale or one payment. Each column is one kind of detail: date, branch, payment, amount.

manas.q: What is the golden rule for laying out data?

children.note: Put short clear headings in row 1. No blank rows or columns inside the data, and no merged cells.
Keep rates and settings (like a commission rate) in their own labelled cells, not typed inside formulas.
Amounts must be real numbers, not text. Text numbers sit on the left of the cell and will not add up.
Click inside the data and press Ctrl+T. The Table grows when you add rows, and formulas copy down by themselves.

manas.q: How do you turn a range into an Excel Table, and why?

children.note: Give it a short name like Sales in Table Design. Then formulas read =SUM(Sales[Amount]) instead of =SUM(D2:D7).
A $ locks a cell so it does not move when you copy a formula. $F$1 stays $F$1 in every row.

manas.q: What does the $ do in $F$1?

children.note: Rate 5% sits in F1. In E2 type =D2*$F$1. For 12,500 the answer is 625. Copied down, Mombasa 8,200 gives 410.
Copied down all six rows, the commissions add up to KES 2,700, which is 5% of 54,000.
Click on the cell reference in the formula and press F4. Each press cycles $F$1, F$1, $F1, F1.
A small set of formulas does most accounting work. Learn these on the example sales data first.
Adds only the rows that meet every condition you give. Format: =SUMIFS(sum range, range1, rule1, range2, rule2).

manas.q: What does SUMIFS do?

children.note: =SUMIFS(D2:D7,B2:B7,"Nairobi",C2:C7,"M-Pesa") gives 20,250 (12,500 + 7,750).
Counts the rows that meet every condition. Same idea as SUMIFS but with no sum range.

manas.q: What does COUNTIFS do?

children.note: =COUNTIFS(C2:C7,"M-Pesa") gives 3.
Looks for an item in one column and returns the matching value from another. Format: =XLOOKUP(what, look in, return from, if not found).

manas.q: What does XLOOKUP do?

children.note: Codes P101 Paracetamol 120, P102 Amoxicillin 450, P103 ORS sachet 35. =XLOOKUP("P102",A2:A4,C2:C4,"Not found") gives 450.
=XLOOKUP("P109",A2:A4,C2:C4,"Not found") gives the words Not found instead of an error.
=VLOOKUP("P102",A2:C4,3,FALSE) also gives 450. The 3 means third column. Older Excel versions only have this one.

manas.q: Why must VLOOKUP end with FALSE?

children.note: FALSE asks for an exact match. Leaving it out lets Excel return a wrong nearby value without warning.
It only looks to the right, and the column number breaks if someone inserts a column. XLOOKUP has neither problem.
=IF(test, answer if true, answer if false). =IF(D2>=10000,"Big","Small") gives Big for 12,500 and Small for 8,200.

manas.q: What is the format of IF?

children.note: Shows your own answer when a formula fails. =IFERROR(D2/E2,0) gives 0 instead of #DIV/0! when E2 is empty.

Excel stores each date as a day count, so you can add and subtract days. Invoice date 15-Mar-2026 plus 30 gives 14-Apr-2026.
=EOMONTH(date, months) gives the last day of a month. For 15-Mar-2026: 0 gives 31-Mar, 1 gives 30-Apr, -1 gives 28-Feb-2026.
